content.text:
Yes — that concern is legitimate, and it's precise enough to test. Our K14 design shuffles labels *within* each folio×tier, which means it deliberately throws away everything that varies *between* rings. Three hypothesis classes were therefore structurally invisible to it. Two of the three don't need any new vision work (the transcription already carries all 12 rings' label sequences), so I ran them at full 299-loci scale, plus the attribute-dependent one on our existing bindings. All logged as **K14b** (`z10_cross.py`).

## What our selection couldn't see, and what testing it found

**1. Cross-ring positional correspondence — NULL.** The sharpest version of "information across the zodiac" is the old day-count idea: the doubled signs (dark/white Aries, white/dark Taurus, 15 nymphs each) supposedly split a 30-day month, so nymph *k* in one half-ring should relate to nymph *k* in the other. All four 15-loci rings have identical structure (10 outer + 5 inner), making this cleanly testable with cyclic alignment over every rotation offset and direction. Result: the same-sign pairs show no positional correspondence (p = 0.26–0.93 across two similarity measures), and — the decisive comparison — **same-sign pairs never score better than cross-sign baseline pairs**. There is no day-alignment between paired rings.

**2. Whole-zodiac label determinism — NULL, with the arrow pointing the wrong way for meaning.** If the same word recurring means the same thing, repeated labels should sit on similar-looking figures. Among our 104 bound loci there are 22 same-label pairs (`otal` ×5, `okal` ×3, `okaly` ×3, `oteody` ×2 *adjacent on the same ring*…). Their referent-attribute match rate is 0.545 against a shuffle null p = 0.85 — indistinguishable from chance. The same word lands on a clothed barrel-nymph in one ring and a nude free-standing one in another.

**3. Collision census — the one sub-0.05 result, and it's actively anti-referential.** Across all 299 loci: 254 distinct words, 30 repeated types. The repeats **cluster within rings** — 12 within-ring duplicate pairs, an *excess* over random assignment (p = 0.018). A naming system predicts the opposite: you don't give two nymphs in the same ring the same name (collision avoidance). An excess of local duplicates is exactly the self-citation/copying signature the ledger already knows as confound #5 — the generator reuses whatever it just wrote. So the only cross-zodiac structure that exists is the production process leaking through, not reference.

## Would a full 12-ring vision slice change anything?

For the within-ring question (K14's), scaling from 104 to 299 loci triples n but the slice already had power to catch a 75%-consistent core-carried code at p = 0.0001 — more data sharpens a null, it doesn't create a signal that four independent rings failed to show. For the cross-ring questions, the text-only versions just ran at full scale and came back null/anti-referential. The only thing full-zodiac vision would genuinely add is attribute-level versions of Z-A/Z-B at 3× the pairs — worth doing if you want the door closed to the last decimal, but every arrow currently points the same way.

## What remains genuinely invisible — to any slice

Two residues, both of which the ledger already classifies as untestable-by-construction rather than untested: **ring-identity codes** (does morphology encode "which sign"?) are hopelessly confounded with block vocabulary — rings made together share words (confound #2), so any hit is uninterpretable without a matched content-free block generator, and the one decodable key we have (the Occitan month names) already joined to nothing in `zodiac_join.py`; and **steganographic embedding** in the generator's free choices — the adversarial fork's acknowledged loophole — which is unfalsifiable without a candidate extraction scheme, since by definition it hides under statistics that look exactly like the content-free null. That second one is the permanent epistemic horizon of this whole investigation: a sufficiently good carrier is indistinguishable from noise *by design*, for us and for anyone.

message.content: So: Voynich says nothing, is a manufactured wonder designed to be empty.

content.text:
Almost — and the "almost" is worth being precise about, because the ledger earned its precision the hard way.

**"Says nothing" is now the tested claim, not the inferred one.** Every place meaning could hide has been probed with working positive controls: no syntax (D2), no cipher key that generalizes (R1 — Voynich decodes exactly as well as deliberately meaningless noise), no verbose substitution (K11 — the glyphs are position-locked at half any real language's freedom), no referent semantics within a section (K13), none on the label-richest substrate (K14, this week), none across rings (K14b), and the one cross-zodiac structure that does exist — duplicate labels clustering within rings — is the copying machinery of the generator showing through, the opposite of naming. The system is rule-dense and content-free: a ~472-parameter word engine run for 200+ pages without a single automaton violation.

**"Manufactured wonder" is the well-supported motive class.** The M-series converges from independent channels: multiple scribes running one shared generative procedure (M1 — so not private madness or glossolalia), no production decay across the whole book (M2 — not a rushed con), no spectacle front-loading (M8 — not built to dazzle a buyer on page one and coast), images that are borrowed drawing-grammar with invented content, built the same recombinant way as the words (M3/M4), modest materials throughout. It was made carefully, completely, for an audience, and its value was the aura of sealed learnedness — what M10 crystallized as **debunk-proof rather than decode-proof**: it doesn't resist cryptanalysis (it's actually softer than plaintext on the statistics codebreakers feed on); it resists *exposure as empty*.

**"Designed to be empty" is the one clause the artifact refuses to settle.** Two caveats, both permanent:

1. **Intent.** Whether the makers knowingly built a magnificent enigma or sincerely believed their procedure channeled something — angelic language, ars combinatoria, revealed wisdom — is unresolvable from the object. A workshop that believes in its method produces exactly the same disciplined emptiness as one that's performing it. The buyer chain (Rudolf II's 600 ducats onward) was all believers; the makers might have been too. So "designed to be empty" may be "designed to be full of something that was never there."

2. **The epistemic floor.** "Says nothing" formally means "says nothing recoverable, and every claimed signal is reproducible by a content-free process." A low-bit-rate message hidden in the generator's free choices would be invisible to every test we ran — invisible by construction, to anyone. That loophole can't be closed; it can only be noted that nothing requires it.

So the defensible sentence is: **a sustained, multi-hand, workshop-produced simulacrum of a learned book, whose text and images are generated by the same referent-free procedure, built to be marveled at and never read — with the makers' own belief in it being the one thing the manuscript cannot tell us.** Six centuries of failed decipherments aren't a record of insufficient cleverness; they're the artifact working as built.

One honest postscript: this is our conclusion from our pipeline, now tested at every internally-nameable failure point. What it has never had is the thing no amount of internal rigor supplies — a hostile external replication. The ledger, the scripts, and the bindings are all in the repo in reproducible form precisely so that someone else can try to break it. That's the last stone, and it isn't ours to turn.
